 1                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Yes, 

 2   Mr. President, thank you very much.

 3                I rise to explain my vote on this 

 4   extremely important piece of legislation to the 

 5   people of the City of Buffalo, especially the 

 6   Fruit Belt neighborhood, a historic residential 

 7   neighborhood in the heart of the City of Buffalo.  

 8   It's right up and adjacent to the Buffalo Niagara 

 9   Medical Campus that is expanding at an 

10   exponential rate, thousands of people being 

11   employed in the downtown corridor that weren't 

12   there in the past, and it's a great thing.  

13                But this has created issues over the 

14   years, issues within the Fruit Belt neighborhood, 

15   the residential neighborhood, as it pertains to 

16   parking.  And so what this bill ultimately does, 

17   it will allow the City of Buffalo to promulgate 

18   a permit system to ensure that residents that 

19   reside in the Fruit Belt neighborhood have that 

20   ability to park where they live.

21                And unfortunately, over the years 

22   it's become very difficult for that to happen.  

23   With the influx of workers and patients and 

24   visitors at the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus, 

25   we've seen a lack of parking in the Fruit Belt 


                                                                4599

 1   neighborhood.  The result has been that 

 2   residents, many of whom live in homes that don't 

 3   have driveways, have to park oftentimes blocks 

 4   away from where they live when they go out to 

 5   perform simple tasks like going grocery shopping 

 6   or driving their children to and from school or 

 7   daycare or other events.  

 8                And at the end of the day, this is a 

 9   transformational bill for the folks in the 

10   Fruit Belt neighborhood and in the Buffalo 

11   Niagara Medical Campus that utilize those 

12   services every single day.

13                This bill took quite a while to get 

14   done, and there are many people to thank.  I want 

15   to thank, first and foremost, the sponsor in the 

16   Assembly, Assemblywoman Crystal Peoples-Stokes, 

17   for her leadership in shepherding this through 

18   the Assembly.  

19                I want to thank Mayor Byron Brown 

20   and his team for really working collaboratively 

21   with other government leaders like Council 

22   President Darius Pridgen and the community 

23   leaders in labor, in the business community, in 

24   the residential community, who came together 

25   countless times, in meeting after meeting, to 


                                                                4600

 1   really work to come up with this solution.

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Can I 

 3   have some order in the house, please.  

 4                Senator Kennedy, excuse me.  

 5                Some order.  Thank you. 

 6                SENATOR KENNEDY:   So there was 

 7   really nothing easy about this bill, because it 

 8   was very complex, the product was very complex, 

 9   and the outcome is a very, very positive one.

10                I want to thank our friends in 

11   organized labor that also came to the table -- 

12   starting with CSEA, CWA, SEIU, and UUP -- who 

13   came to the table, worked through these issues 

14   and communicated, which was the most important 

15   thing.

16                I also want to give a special thanks 

17   to the leadership in my house, Senator Andrea 

18   Stewart-Cousins, for prioritizing this, working 

19   across the aisle with the committee chair of 

20   Transportation, Senator Joe Robach, also Senator 

21   Patrick Gallivan and the leadership of Senator 

22   Klein, Senator Flanagan, for bringing this to the 

23   floor today.

24                 I vote aye, Mr. President.  Thank 

25   you.

24                SENATOR GOLDEN:   Thank you, 

25   Mr. President.  I rise briefly to explain this 


                                                                4603

 1   great bill and thank my colleagues for voting for 

 2   it.  

 3                We lose millions of dollars here in 

 4   this great nation each and every year because of 

 5   cybersecurity and identity theft.  We've been 

 6   working very closely with the Manhattan District 

 7   Attorney, Cy Vance, on a comprehensive bill to 

 8   address these issues.  This bill identifies many 

 9   new activities as identity theft and creates a 

10   graduated series of penalties based on the actual 

11   or potential damages by the number of persons and 

12   properties affected and the dollar figures, how 

13   it graduates.

14                Also the bill sets a new series of 

15   definitions and crimes related to the use of 

16   skimmer devices, such as cloned remotes, schemes 

17   to defraud through digital means.  They came into 

18   my community in one weekend and emptied that 

19   community out of a million dollars in about 

20   12 hours, going into six or seven different 

21   stores with these skimmer devices.  

22                It's expanding that definition of 

23   illegal theft of computer related materials to 

24   cover positioning systems and personal 

25   preferences of machine operations, and making 


                                                                4604

 1   such things as theft of vehicle access codes 

 2   subject to larceny and criminal possession of 

 3   criminal property provisions.

 4                That's just a few of the different 

 5   upgrades that we will do to bring cybersecurity 

 6   and identity theft into the 21st century.  We 

 7   need to get these laws passed, we need to get 

 8   them on the books, and we need to stop the 

 9   billions and billions of dollars that we lose 

10   each and every year through identity theft and 

11   through cybersecurity.  

12                I vote aye, and I thank my 

13   colleagues for voting aye as well.
